sentences.text: Martha vicinum senem habet. Vicinus bonus est. Senex in domo parva habitat. Nomen ei Petrus est.
sentences.english: Martha has an old neighbour. The neighbour is good. The old man lives in a small house. His name is Peter.

sentences.text: Petrus fessus est, et aquam non habet. Heri quoque aquam non habuit.
sentences.english: Peter is tired, and he does not have water. Yesterday too he did not have water.

sentences.text: Heri Marcus et Samuel ad domum senis venerunt. Senem in porta viderunt.
sentences.english: Yesterday Marcus and Samuel came to the old man's house. They saw the old man at the door.

sentences.text: Salve, Petre! Quomodo vales?
sentences.english: Hello, Peter! How are you?
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Non bene valeo, Marce. Fessus sum, et aquam non habeo.
sentences.english: I am not well, Marcus. I am tired, and I do not have water.
sentences.speaker: senex

sentences.text: Aquam non habes? Ubi est aqua?
sentences.english: You do not have water? Where is the water?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Aqua longe est. Ego non ambulo.
sentences.english: The water is far away. I do not walk.
sentences.speaker: senex

sentences.text: Nos te iuvamus! Aquam tibi damus.
sentences.english: We help you! We give you water.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Marcus et Samuel ad aquam eunt. Aquam habent, et ad domum senis eunt. Tandem senex aquam habet.
sentences.english: Marcus and Samuel go to the water. They have water, and they go to the old man's house. At last the old man has water.

sentences.text: Gratias vobis ago, pueri! Vos boni estis.
sentences.english: Thank you, boys! You are good.
sentences.speaker: senex

sentences.text: Libenter te iuvamus, Petre. Nunc aquam habes.
sentences.english: We gladly help you, Peter. Now you have water.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Heri in domo fui, et aquam non habui. Hodie vos hic estis. Deus vos amat.
sentences.english: Yesterday I was at home, and I did not have water. Today you are here. God loves you.
sentences.speaker: senex

sentences.text: Marcus dixit: Cras iterum venimus. Iterum aquam damus. Senex dixit: Gratias Deo ago.
sentences.english: Marcus said: Tomorrow we come again. We give water again. The old man said: I give thanks to God.

sentences.text: Postea Marcus ad domum Marthae venit. Martha Marcum videt.
sentences.english: Afterwards Marcus comes to Martha's house. Martha sees Marcus.

sentences.text: Ubi fuisti, Marce?
sentences.english: Where were you, Marcus?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: In domo Petri fui, avia. Aquam ei dedi.
sentences.english: I was at Peter's house, grandmother. I gave him water.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Bene! Petrus vicinus bonus est. Tu quoque puer bonus es.
sentences.english: Good! Peter is a good neighbour. You are a good boy too.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Samuel mecum fuit. Samuel quoque senem iuvit.
sentences.english: Samuel was with me. Samuel helped the old man too.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Samuel amicus bonus est. Vos boni estis. Panem vobis do.
sentences.english: Samuel is a good friend. You are good. I give you bread.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Martha panem Marco dat. Postea Samuel venit. Martha dixit: Ecce panis! Panem edite.
sentences.english: Martha gives bread to Marcus. Afterwards Samuel comes. Martha said: Here is bread! Eat the bread.

sentences.text: Marcus et Samuel panem edunt. Fessi sunt, sed bene valent. Multi homines boni in urbe sunt. Vicinus senex quoque bonus est.
sentences.english: They are tired, but they are well. There are many good people in the town. The old neighbour is good too.

sentences.text: Petrus canem habet. Canis bonus est. Canis in via ambulat, et senem amat.
sentences.english: Peter has a dog. The dog is good. The dog walks on the road, and loves the old man.

sentences.text: Hodie Petrus dicit: Caput meum dolet. Anna nutrix est. Anna senem iuvat.
sentences.english: Today Peter says: My head hurts. Anna is a nurse. Anna helps the old man.

sentences.text: Anna, caput meum dolet. Quid facio?
sentences.english: Anna, my head hurts. What do I do?
sentences.speaker: senex

sentences.text: Aquam bibe, Petre! Aqua bona est. Hodie in domo manere bonum est.
sentences.english: Drink water, Peter! Water is good. It is good to stay at home today.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Gratias tibi ago, Anna. Tu nutrix bona es. Marcus et Samuel quoque boni sunt.
sentences.english: Thank you, Anna. You are a good nurse. Marcus and Samuel are good too.
sentences.speaker: senex
